page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual instance within the Enhanced family, driven by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs running on a single physical core across two hardware threads, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance relies on KVM virtualization and supports x86_64 vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI. Networking is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no local instance storage is bundled, necessitating attached cloud storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations show average single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1500.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1847.58, and gzip compression throughput of 27.77 GB/sec. However, overall multi-core and aggregate throughput measures place in the lower quartile due to the two-thread, single-core physical constraint. Geekbench multi-core registers at 1751.0, PassMark CPU reaches 2950.81, and database operations score 977.34. Memory throughput shows uncached 256MB read and write bandwidths of 14.01 GB/sec and 12.76 GB/sec respectively, while static web serving achieves 3.33 GB/sec.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency standpoint, this instance provides dedicated execution units that prevent noisy-neighbor contention for light computational tasks. The absence of integrated disks and GPUs keeps resource overhead low, though workloads requiring sustained parallel compute or memory-intensive caching will encounter bottlenecks. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.large is best matched for single-threaded utilities, microservices, lightweight web servers, edge application gateways, and non-concurrent background workers.

Configured with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface, it operates on KVM without included local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results display balanced single-core execution with a Geekbench score of 1500.0 and single-thread gzip speeds of 27.77 GB/sec.
